explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: H100 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index; 1-yr contract and spot)
indicators.value: $2.75/hr index (+5.4% 7d) Sep 30 final, no Oct 1 print yet; H200 $3.37 (+2.1% 7d, revised up from $3.29 intraday); MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%); H100-hyperscaler $7.20; RunPod H100 SXM $3.49/$2.69, Lambda $3.99-4.29 unchanged; Nebius H100 list +17% from Oct 1; CME futures launch pushed past Oct 5 (CFTC review to Nov 9)
indicators.why: This is the marginal clearing price of installed AI compute and the most direct public read on whether capacity is being discounted; it is published daily and becomes a CME-listed futures contract on Oct 5, 2026.
indicators.watch: Bearish flip if the Silicon Data H100 index holds below ~$2.00/hr for a month, if spot trades below the one-year contract rate (inversion), or if the CME H100 curve lists in steep (>15%) backwardation; the Oct-2025 trough of $1.70 is the floor to remember.
indicators.note: Oct 1 02:30 UTC: Silicon Data's pages still carry the Sep 30 print - SDH100RT $2.75 (+5.4% 7d), the three-month high set Sep 28-30; the only change since the midday read is H200, now $3.37 (+2.1% 7d) versus $3.29 earlier in the day, so Hopper's memory-rich variant firmed too. MI300X $2.63 (+0.4%), H100-hyperscaler $7.20 (+0.3%). RunPod and Lambda lists unchanged; Nebius's +17% H100 rise is live from today. Visibility leg unchanged: the CME/Silicon Data H100 (GPU1) and B200 (GPU2) futures will not list Oct 5 - the CFTC extended its review 45 days to Nov 9 (FinanceFeeds, Sep 29); each contract is 730 GPU-hours, cash-settled on the Silicon Data index, monthly out to 36 months. No public forward curve this quarter. Micron's print overnight (DRAM ASP +high-teens QoQ, HBM 2027 'vast majority' contracted at significantly higher prices) is the input-cost side of the same story: rent is rising because the parts are.

indicators.name: B200 / Blackwell rental price, $/GPU-hour (on-demand)
indicators.value: Silicon Data B200 $5.78 (-0.2% 7d) vs $5.88 Sep 29; B300 $6.78 (-0.3%) back to its soft print; RunPod B200 $5.98/$6.79, B300 $6.94/$7.89, Lambda B200 $6.69-6.99 unchanged; B200/H100 ~2.10x; Nebius B200 +19%, B300 +21% from Oct 1; CoreWeave puts Vera Rubin NVL72 into production (Sep 30)
indicators.why: Blackwell is where new supply lands, so this is the first place a glut would show; if B200 rates fell toward H100 rates while Rubin ships, capacity would be outrunning demand.
indicators.watch: Bearish if tier-1 neocloud B200 on-demand drops below ~$4.50/hr, if the B200/H100 price ratio compresses below ~2x, or if lead times for 8-GPU Blackwell nodes fall to same-week availability.
indicators.note: Sep 30: B200 index $5.78 (-0.2% 7d), down 1.7% on the day from $5.88, and B300 slipped back to $6.78 (-0.3% 7d) after Monday's recovery to $6.92. With H100 rising and B200 easing, the ratio narrowed to ~2.10x - the closest it has been to the 2x flip line, though still above it and B200 is far above the $4.50 trigger. Worth pairing with the day's other datapoint: CoreWeave says it is the first cloud running Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 at production scale, with Cognition the first customer (Fully Connected, Sep 30), so Rubin is now shipping while Blackwell spot softens - exactly the combination the watch line describes, in its earliest form. List prices at RunPod and Lambda are unchanged and Nebius's Oct 1 Blackwell rises (+19%/+21%) still stand. No Oct 1 index print at 02:30 UTC.

indicators.name: Legacy-GPU residual value: used H100 prices, A100/H100 rates and booked useful lives
indicators.value: A100 index $1.58/hr (+0.6% 7d) Sep 30 final, above the $1.50 trigger; A100-hyperscaler $3.76 (+0.3%); used H100 SXM ~$18-27K by age vs $30K list (Jun); MSFT/Meta lives unchanged
indicators.why: Depreciation is the biggest cost in a GPU cloud; if old chips still earn money the 5-6 year accounting lives hold and no write-downs are coming, whereas collapsing used-H100 prices would be the first hard evidence of oversupply.
indicators.watch: Bearish if 8-GPU H100 servers trade below ~50% of new-build cost on the secondary market, if A100/H100 rental rates fall below ~$1.50/hr, or if any hyperscaler extends server lives beyond 6 years to flatter earnings; also watch for Hopper impairments at neoclouds.
indicators.note: Sep 30 final print: A100 index ticked up to $1.58 (+0.6% 7d) from $1.57, 8 cents above the trigger; A100-hyperscaler $3.76 (+0.3%); RunPod A100 SXM $1.39/$1.59 and Lambda A100 $1.99-2.79 unchanged. No new used-H100 prints, impairments or useful-life changes found; latest reference (Mercatus, Jun 23) has 18-30-month-old H100s at 75-85% of a $30K list. Hopper rental +5.4% on the week, H200 +2.1%, and Nebius's 17% H100 rise from Oct 1 all support residuals. Nothing from Micron's call changes the depreciation picture; if anything, rising HBM prices for 2027 make installed Hopper (with its already-paid-for memory) relatively cheaper to keep running.

indicators.name: All-in AI data-center build cost, $ per GW (with GPUs / ex-GPUs)
indicators.value: ~$47B/GW Vera Rubin (≈$32B racks + ≈$15B shell/power/cooling); ~$60B/GW gas-powered campus (Orennia); Project Jupiter $165B for 2.45 GW ≈ $67B/GW all-in; TCS Hyderabad $7.4B for 1 GW ex-GPU shell; CDC Gregadoo (Wagga Wagga) A$15B ≈ US$10B for a 'gigawatt-scale' ex-GPU campus, concept phase
indicators.why: Cost per GW sets the revenue a campus must earn per GPU-hour to clear its cost of capital; rising cost means supply is constrained (good for rental prices) but raises the bar for returns and the size of the debt stack.
indicators.watch: Discounting signal if Nvidia rack ASPs or $/GW start falling (Nvidia gross margin guided below ~72%, rack prices cut) while rental $/hr does not rise; bubble-risk signal if ex-GPU cost (power, shell, turbines) keeps inflating faster than rental rates.
indicators.note: One datapoint added, and it is Australian: Infratil-backed CDC Data Centres is planning a A$15B, gigawatt-scale campus at Gregadoo outside Wagga Wagga (ABC Sep 29; Region Riverina and BeBeez Sep 30). CDC's own site calls it 'concept phase', transmission-level grid connection, closed-loop cooling, no capacity or timeline disclosed. At roughly US$10B for about a GW of shell, power and cooling it sits between TCS Hyderabad (~$7.4B/GW) and the ~$15B/GW US ex-GPU figure - consistent with regional-Australian land and power being cheaper than Texas, not with costs falling. Prior datapoints unchanged: Oracle's Project Jupiter ($165B for 2.45 GW, ~$67B/GW, force majeure Sep 24) and the Orennia $60B/GW gas-campus benchmark. Memory input costs still rising (see memory_prices).

indicators.name: Server DRAM / HBM contract price momentum (QoQ) and DRAM spot
indicators.value: Micron FQ4 (Sep 30): rev $54.23B vs $51.5B est, non-GAAP GM 87.0%, DRAM ASP +high-teens QoQ, NAND ASP ~+30%; FQ1 guide $61.5B ±$1.5B at ~86.25% GM ('low point for FY27'); 'vast majority' of CY2027 HBM bits contracted at significantly higher YoY prices; supply-constrained through 2028; H1 FY27 capex ~$25B, H2 higher; TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121%; DDR5 16Gb spot $57.90 (Sep 30, +0.12%), Oct 1 print due ~18:10 Taipei
indicators.why: Memory is the tightest physical input to AI servers (HBM is 25-30% of a Rubin rack) and contract prices are negotiated quarterly, so this is the earliest cyclical input to turn; a price rollover would precede GPU discounting.
indicators.watch: Bearish when server DRAM or HBM contract prices go negative QoQ, when 2027 HBM4 contracts are signed at lower prices, or when DRAMeXchange DDR5 spot falls >20% from peak; also watch whether CSPs start cutting memory per system (TrendForce now says GPU makers are evaluating 8-Hi instead of 12-Hi HBM stacks), which is the buyers' cost response. Near term: Samsung Q3 prelim Oct 8 (consensus cut to ~107T won); TrendForce 4Q26 contract settlement; Micron's FQ1 print in December against an 86.25% guide it calls the FY27 low.
indicators.note: Micron's fiscal Q4 (Sep 30, after the close) is the hard confirmation the memory leg wanted. Revenue $54.23B (+31% QoQ on a 14-week quarter, +379% YoY) against ~$51.5B consensus; non-GAAP gross margin 87.0% (+210bp QoQ) vs 45.7% a year ago; non-GAAP EPS $33.42 vs $31.82; operating cash flow $43.97B on net capex $10.77B. The pricing lines matter most: DRAM ASP up high-teens percent QoQ on mid-single-digit bit growth, NAND ASP up ~30% on ~10% bits, DRAM revenue $39.8B and data-center SSD nearly $10B (10x YoY). Guide: FQ1 FY27 revenue $61.5B ±$1.5B, GM ~86.25% (which management called the low point for fiscal 2027, with ~$1B of incentive-comp and start-up cost flowing through), EPS $38.15 ±$1.00 non-GAAP, net capex ~$11.5B; H1 FY27 capex ~$25B with H2 higher, mostly cleanroom construction for late-2028 capacity. HBM: agreements in place for the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bit supply at 'significantly higher' YoY prices, NV-HBM custom HBM4E with Nvidia, and DRAM and NAND both described as supply-constrained through 2028; 26 multi-year customer agreements cover >35% of revenue through 2030 with ~$150B of RPO at set pricing. The stock did nothing - flat at $1,065.11 on the close, +0.4% after hours - which says the beat was priced, not that the cycle turned. DRAM spot: TrendForce's Oct 1 update was not yet posted at 02:30 UTC; the Sep 30 print stands (DDR5 16Gb $57.90 +0.12%, DDR4 16Gb $83.69 +0.03%, DDR4 8Gb $46.32 flat), with NAND wafers the one soft leg (-2.45% w/w, 'buying weak') - and Micron just said NAND contract ASP rose ~30% in the quarter, so spot softness is at the margin, not the core. Contract-side: TrendForce 2027 HBM ASP +121% YoY unchanged.

indicators.name: Power constraint: ERCOT interconnection queue, gas-turbine backlog and lead times
indicators.value: 474 GW ERCOT queue (~90% data centers); Texas TCEQ permit freeze since Sep 21, compliance report due Oct 19; BNEF: 49.8 GW delayed; GE Vernova 116 GW backlog, ~20 GW/yr output, new orders land ~2030-31; Oracle force majeure on 2.45 GW Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 2027); US Senate blocks Ratepayer Protection Act 57-43 (Sep 30); Dover DE 18-month data-center moratorium
indicators.why: Power, not chips, is now the binding constraint on new capacity, which keeps installed GPUs scarce and rental prices firm; it also reveals how much announced demand is speculative once regulators force projects to prove financing.
indicators.watch: ERCOT files its Batch Zero eligibility-verification and community-impact reports by Dec 10, 2026 for the Dec 17 PUCT open meeting, with RFIs going out Aug-Sep and cure periods Oct-Nov: large queue withdrawals (BNEF flags 49.8 GW at risk) would show phantom demand. Turbine slot cancellations or resales, falling data-center PPA prices, or turbine prices retreating from the $600/kW 2027 forecast would signal the build is slowing. Nearer: TCEQ compliance report Oct 19, Project Jupiter air-permit decision Nov 23.
indicators.note: No new queue or backlog numbers; the Texas freeze stands with TCEQ's report due Oct 19 and ERCOT's audit still targeted for mid-December. What moved Sep 30 was the politics of who pays for power. The US Senate failed 57-43 (60 needed) to advance Sen. Husted's Ratepayer Protection Act, which would have made state regulators decide whether data centers bear the incremental cost of grid build-out; the House had passed it 417-3 on Sep 16, and Democrats blocked it as 'toothless', pushing a GRID Savings Act that would make data centers pay full upgrade costs (KSL/AP, Sep 30). Either version raises the ex-GPU cost of a campus; neither passed, so the status quo - ratepayers absorbing part of the bill - holds for now, but both parties are now campaigning on making data centers pay. At the local level Dover, Delaware passed a unanimous 18-month moratorium on data-center applications citing rising power prices (Delaware Public Media, Sep 30) - small, but the pattern of towns pre-emptively closing the door is what turns a queue into phantom demand. Prior items unchanged: Oracle's Sep 24 force majeure on Project Jupiter (gas pipeline to Feb 1, 2027, air permit Nov 23); GE Vernova 116 GW backlog against ~20 GW/yr output; Exelon's ~40% cut to 'high-probability' data-center load.

indicators.name: Hyperscaler capex vs cloud backlog (RPO) growth, and capex as % of cloud revenue
indicators.value: Anthropic prospectus: $518B of compute commitments over 7-10 yrs (Broadcom leases $161.2B, Google $111.1B, Amazon $110B, xAI/Nvidia up to $84.5B, Microsoft $31.4B, AMD $20B+), ~80% non-cancelable; Oracle RPO $664B but force majeure on Project Jupiter; Micron: ~$150B RPO, 26 multi-year deals >35% of revenue through 2030, H1 FY27 capex ~$25B; SoftBank $11.1B HY bonds for OpenAI; Goldman: US hyperscaler capex $1.4T in 2027
indicators.why: Capex is the supply side and RPO is the contracted demand side; as long as backlog grows faster than capex the build is pre-sold, but capex above 100% of cloud revenue with negative free cash flow means the cycle is now funded by debt and equity and is sensitive to any demand wobble.
indicators.watch: Bearish if RPO growth decelerates below capex growth for two quarters, if 2027 capex consensus (+57% per Morgan Stanley) gets cut or 'digestion' language appears, or if backlog concentration in a few AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic) produces a cancellation or renegotiation; Oracle's Project Jupiter force majeure is the first payment-deferral mechanism triggered on a Stargate site - watch whether it spreads.
indicators.note: Micron added a supplier-side version of the backlog ledger overnight: 26 multi-year strategic customer agreements covering more than 35% of revenue through 2030, roughly $150B of remaining performance obligations at determined pricing, and the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bits already contracted at higher prices - against H1 FY27 capex of ~$25B and a higher H2 (Yahoo call highlights, Sep 30). That is the same shape as the cloud ledger - buyers locking in supply years out, supplier spending into it - and it tells you the hyperscalers are still signing, not pausing. Demand-side ledger otherwise unchanged: Anthropic's $518B of compute commitments (~80% non-cancelable, ~$2T IPO marketing expected from mid-October), Oracle's $664B RPO with Project Jupiter under force majeure, SoftBank's $11.1B HY bonds for OpenAI. The counter-signal is in the financing leg (see neocloud_credit): Barclays says data-center securitisations now trade with corporate AI debt rather than the ABS market, and 2026 issuance is running below 2025. Next hard data: late-October hyperscaler prints.

indicators.name: Neocloud financing: CoreWeave loan/bond spreads, CDS, vendor backstops, customer concentration
indicators.value: CoreWeave $4.2B 2.875% converts (closed Sep 24); Lambda $926M TLB at SOFR+300, Baa2 (Sep 22); CoreWeave loans still ~SOFR+550, debt $35.1B at Jun 30; data-center ABS $11.9B YTD vs $15.5B in 2025, hyperscaler ABS ~150bp over 5-yr Treasury (+16bp YoY), corporate AI debt ~165bp over SOFR (+31bp); CleanSpark/Meta $2.23B 5-yr secured notes ~8.5% with concessions; CRWV $87.12 close Sep 30 (+1.4%), 52-wk $60.55-153.20
indicators.why: Neoclouds are the levered marginal builder of GPU capacity; their cost of debt, covenants and dependence on Nvidia backstops show whether lenders still believe rental prices will cover depreciation, and they are the first place a compute-price decline turns into forced selling.
indicators.watch: Escalation if new deals price above SOFR+600 or 11% yields, CDS above 1,000bp, deals pulled or downsized, Nvidia's rent-back backstop extended to tier-1 neoclouds, or a top customer (CoreWeave's A/B/C are 36%/26%/10% of revenue) renegotiates; improvement if spreads retrace toward the April 9.75% level or if CoreWeave can tap convertible/equity-linked money on Nebius-like terms.
indicators.note: No new neocloud debt priced, but the securitised leg got a read. The Real Deal (via Yahoo, Sep 30) quotes Barclays' Elana Lipchak: data-center ABS/CMBS now trade 'less correlated with broader ABS or CMBS and more correlated with all the debt supply on the AI infrastructure trade from corporates' - hyperscaler-tenant ABS at ~150bp over 5-yr Treasuries (16bp wider YoY) and corporate AI debt ~165bp over SOFR (31bp wider) while the rest of the ABS market has tightened; 2026 data-center ABS issuance is $11.9B YTD against $15.5B for all of 2025, and Fed Chair Warsh is on record that 'the competition for capital is real'. The Information's version (paywalled, headline only) says CleanSpark's $2.23B Meta-tenant bond cleared only with big investor concessions - that deal was marketed near 8.5% on Sep 17. So: still open, but lenders are pricing data-center paper as AI credit risk, not real estate. CRWV closed $87.12 (+1.4%) Sep 30, $87.25 after hours, ~43% off the high; the Fully Connected product day (Vera Rubin NVL72 in production, Forge, Vera CPU) and CEO Intrator's 'regulation won't reduce demand' line are unchanged from the last read. Signal stays neutral: top-tier cost of money eased in September, the securitised and secured stacks are getting dearer at the margin.

indicators.name: Nvidia data-center revenue growth, gross margin and customer concentration
indicators.value: DC rev $89.0B +117% YoY (Q2 FY27), GM 75.0%, Q3 guide $108B at 74%; one direct customer >=10% (16%); five customers = 70% of receivables; supply commitments $279B; OpenAI Ohio backstop cut to <$120B; $150B buyback added Sep 28 ($235B remaining); CME GPU futures delayed to at least Nov 9 (CFTC); Micron: NV-HBM custom HBM4E, 2027 HBM priced 'significantly higher'; glass-substrate packaging targeted 2028
indicators.why: Nvidia's margin is the purest read on whether GPUs are being discounted at the source, and its concentration plus growing vendor-financing (backstops, campus guarantees) shows how much of demand is circular.
indicators.watch: Bearish if gross margin is guided below ~72% for more than one quarter, data-center revenue grows <5% sequentially, three-customer concentration exceeds 60% in the 10-Q, DSO climbs past 60 days, or backstop commitments expand beyond the $108.5B disclosed; Q3 FY27 report due ~Nov 2026.
indicators.note: Operating figures unchanged from the Aug 26 10-Q and the Sep 28 buyback. The overnight read-through is on the cost side: Micron has the vast majority of calendar-2027 HBM bits contracted at 'significantly higher' YoY prices and is building a custom HBM4E part (NV-HBM) for Nvidia's next GPUs and NVLink Fusion - so Nvidia's biggest bought-in input is getting dearer into Rubin, and the 74% Q3 guide already has to absorb that. Nvidia is also reportedly pushing suppliers (AUO, Innolux, GTOC, TPK, SCHMID) to have glass substrates ready within two years for possible 2028 volume, a sign CoWoS-style packaging is the next bottleneck after HBM (TrendForce, Sep 30). Rubin revenue is live: CoreWeave is running Vera Rubin NVL72 at production scale with Cognition as first customer. The public forward curve remains off the table (CFTC review to Nov 9). Anthropic's prospectus puts up to $84.5B of xAI/Nvidia capacity in its $518B of commitments, mostly cancelable on 90 days' notice. Next data: Q3 FY27 print ~Nov.
